idea: SeguridadMesh is an AI video analytics overlay for municipal serenazgo camera networks in Peru that detects street-level incidents—such as assaults, thefts, and traffic accidents—in real time and instantly alerts operators with minimal distraction.

selected_gap.title: Incident detection tailored to Peruvian serenazgo contexts
selected_gap.why_now: Municipalities increase security budgets but generic analytics miss local crime patterns, causing operator fatigue and slow response.
selected_gap.evidence_needed: Interview serenazgo operators at 3 municipalities to catalog undetected incident types; prototype a detection model on sample footage and compare to manual monitoring.
selected_gap.risk: Competitors may adapt with localized models; requires continuous data collection.

friedman_scores.note: Founder background unknown; no clear domain expertise in Peruvian public safety.
TAM is small: municipal security budgets in Peru are limited, likely < $200M.
High pain from crime and slow response, but municipal budgets are constrained.
Generic video analytics exist but few tailored to Peru; local adaptation is an advantage.
Founder's personal motivation not disclosed; assume moderate.
AI advances and increasing security budgets make it timely.
Verkada and others show success in similar spaces, but B2G in Peru is distinct.
Navigating B2G sales cycles requires long-term commitment.
Software scales, but each municipality requires customization and trust-building.
Vertical AI for public safety is a promising and underserved niche.

yc_rule_scores.criterion: Do not wait for the perfect idea
yc_rule_scores.note: Specific idea with concrete target; good to start.
Claims to understand serenazgo workflow but no evidence yet.

yc_rule_scores.criterion: Build at the edge of AI
yc_rule_scores.note: Uses AI but not cutting-edge research; edge is domain adaptation.
Sells 'proactive response' but pricing is license-based, not outcome-based.
Aiming for entire Peru serenazgo system is ambitious.
No structured approach to failure outlined.
Public sector fits perfectly: low trust, high need for expertise.
Focus is on software product, not process.
Must validate with real municipalities before scaling.
Annual license per camera is per unit, but not per result.

yc_rule_scores.criterion: Do not bolt AI onto legacy
yc_rule_scores.note: Overlay on existing cameras is acceptable; not legacy reengineering.

yc_rule_scores.criterion: Cover domain, model, and operations fluency
yc_rule_scores.note: Domain fluency lacking until customer interviews done.

vc_rubric_scores.rationale: Founder not described; likely lacks deep domain expertise in Peruvian public safety or serenazgo operations.
Total addressable market is small: Peru's 1800+ municipalities have limited security budgets, unlikely to exceed $200M.
Moated by localized data and workflow integration, but initial prototype not demonstrated; competitors could replicate.
No evidence of customer interviews, pilots, or letters of intent; pure idea stage.
Annual B2G license with high margins, but LTV:CAC unknown and long sales cycles may erode economics.
Faces large incumbents (Honeywell, Bosch) and startups; local adaptation is weak moat if they decide to enter.
No financial data; assuming reasonable burn but slow revenue ramp typical for B2G.
High risk from corruption, regulatory hurdles, and long procurement cycles; many failure points.

decision: Do not pursue this idea as a primary venture due to weak market size, no traction, and high B2G risk. Consider it only as a side project if founder has direct insider access.
next_experiments: Interview serenazgo operators at 3 municipalities to catalog undetected incident types and validate pain.
Prototype a detection model on sample footage (e.g., YouTube videos of Peruvian streets) and compare accuracy to manual monitoring.
kill_criteria: No interest or willingness to pilot from first 3 municipalities after interviews.
Prototype accuracy below 70% for key incident types.
Evidence that existing solutions (e.g., generic analytics) satisfy operators.
_iteration_one_liner: We give serenazgo operators an AI copilot that detects street crimes in real-time on their existing cameras, so they can dispatch officers faster instead of waiting for phone calls.
